---
title: Files
description: How Marfa keeps a file's bytes once, however many items name them, who may read them, and where the copies live.
---

A file in Marfa comes in two parts. The bytes are a **blob**, stored once under a hash of their content. The file itself is an **item**, which names the blob by that hash and carries everything else: a title, a media type, the size of an image.

Keeping them apart stores the same bytes once however many items use them, and keeps an item small enough for every device to hold.

## A blob and the item that names it

To add a file, upload its bytes, then create an item that names the hash Marfa answers:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa blobs upload inventory.txt
```

```text
stored sha256:7fc0ba0d4e6818ccf1f3eae53ed1ce059625672ff5438d0ab59b12ab6e0305ef (64 bytes, text/plain)
```

</Terminal>

A file item is an item of `core.file` or a type that inherits from it, such as `core.file.image` for a photo or `core.file.webpage` for a saved page. Its `blob_ref` is the hash, always written `sha256:` and 64 hex digits:

```http title="Request"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "type": "core.file",
  "properties": {
    "title": "Flat inventory",
    "blob_ref": "sha256:7fc0ba0d4e6818ccf1f3eae53ed1ce059625672ff5438d0ab59b12ab6e0305ef",
    "mime_type": "text/plain"
  }
}
```

Marfa sets the item's `size_bytes` from the bytes it holds, so no writer has to. The same bytes uploaded again answer the same hash and are stored once, so two items can name one blob. [Handle files](/build/handle-files) walks through uploading, downloading and replacing a file, and attaching one to another item.

## Find a file by what it says

**Marfa reads the text inside files**: a PDF's pages, a document's words, the words in a scanned receipt. It writes what it reads onto the file item as `extracted_text`, and search matches it like any other text. Seconds after the upload above, a search for `oak` finds the inventory. An image also gains its `width` and `height`, and a recording its `duration`.

The owner can turn text reading off, or OCR on images alone, in [Settings](/run/settings).

## Who may read a blob

**Knowing a hash isn't enough** to read the bytes. A credential reads a blob through an item that names it: if you can read a file item, you can read its blob. A hash elsewhere in an item counts too, such as an image embedded in a note's Markdown body.

A reference counts only if whoever wrote it had uploaded the bytes or could already read them, so naming a hash you found somewhere gives you nothing. A file item can't name such a hash at all: the write is refused with `404 blob_not_found`. Upload the bytes with the same credential first, as [Handle files](/build/handle-files#point-an-item-at-the-bytes) shows.

A blob you may not read answers `404 blob_not_found`, as a missing one does. That holds even for a blob you uploaded, until an item names it.

[Download a blob](/api-reference/blobs/downloadBlob) answers the bytes, and takes a `Range` for part of them. For a page or a player that can't send a credential, `marfa blobs url` or [Get a blob URL](/api-reference/blobs/getBlobUrl) answers a **signed link** that works without one. It lasts an hour by default, and `ttl_seconds` sets up to seven days.

## Where the copies live

Every instance keeps its blobs on the disk beside the server, and records each copy in its **copy record**. Two more stores can hold copies:

- **The backup folder**, once [backups](/run/back-up-and-restore) are on, gets a copy of every file.
- **An S3-compatible object store**, once [added](/run/run-on-a-server#an-object-store), gets a second copy of every blob, and a signed link then points straight at the store.

<FileStorage />

The instance checks the copies regularly and replaces one that's missing or damaged. `marfa blobs copies` answers the stores that hold a blob and when each copy was last found intact, and `marfa blobs delete-copy`, with `blobs.manage`, removes one store's copy where enough live copies remain.

A blob stays as long as something names it, including an item in the bin or an earlier version of an item. Once nothing does, Marfa removes it after `blob_cleanup_grace_seconds`, a day by default.

The rules behind this page are in the [blobs](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/blobs.md) and [stores](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/stores.md) chapters of the contract.
